verdict_A: NOT FOUND (provisional). No source found stating a finite-sample impossibility/possibility frontier for scale-and-shift-equivariant intervals under stratified SRSWOR over a max-share class, nor the multiple-choice-knapsack form (product of per-stratum pi_h(k) vs sum of capacities a_h(k)), nor Theorem 3a/3b, the (R_h,N_h) level bound, or the general (v_h,kappa_h)-monotone-class / Lambda0-and-v0 form (ceil(1/v0) simultaneously degenerate strata). Ingredients exist separately: (i) single-sample iid threshold n>=log2(2/alpha) with shift-invariant CI and Lanke-1974 impossibility for n<log2(1/alpha) (Paul & Kuchibhotla arXiv:2403.06357, Remark 1; read in full text); (ii) 'worst case = k equal nonzero variances' extremal structure (Bakirov & Szekely 2006; Szekely arXiv math/0610838 Thm 3.1, snippet) -- the same extremal shape as your two-point populations, but Gaussian/symmetric iid, no finite population; (iii) finite-sample size-controllability iff-conditions in Gaussian regression with leverage (Potscher & Preinerstorfer arXiv:2412.17470, read in full text; no finite-population/strata/cluster content); (iv) asymptotic max-share/Lindeberg conditions: Hajek 1960 condition max(x-mu)^2/(v*min(n,N-n))->0 (seen in arXiv:2301.08324 Thm A.2), Bickel & Freedman 1984 Lindeberg conditions for stratified sampling (abstract), Carter-Schnepel-Steigerwald 2017 effective number of clusters, Djogbenou-MacKinnon-Nielsen 2019, Sasaki-Wang arXiv:2308.10138 (abstracts only). These are asymptotic sufficient conditions, not finite-sample frontiers. Gleser-Hwang/Dufour/Bahadur-Savage supply the proof technique, not the result. Identity (I) (kappa_st = max_h v_h kappa_h) was not found stated anywhere but is elementary. Hansen 2026 RES (doi:10.1093/restud/rdag050) was available as abstract only (paywalled); its abstract (Cauchy-bounded worst-case coverage, single treated cluster, regression) does not suggest finite-population or stratified results, but full text unverified.
verdict_B: PARTLY. The qualitative idea -- pooling a few heterogeneous groups restores valid inference where each group alone cannot -- is in print: Ibragimov & Mueller 2010/2016 (t-test on q>=2 asymptotically Gaussian group estimators valid at alpha<=0.083 for all q, 0.10 for q<=14, via Bakirov-Szekely) and Canay-Romano-Shaikh 2017 (sign-change tests with few clusters), plus the single-sample threshold n>=log2(2/alpha) (Paul & Kuchibhotla; Lanke 1974). NOT found: the finite-population statement that stratified SRSWOR with fewer than log2(2/alpha) draws per stratum can carry a scale-free finite-sample guarantee over a max-share class when strata are pooled, the explicit frontier, or the numerical example (G=24, N=2000, m=4, alpha=0.1, frontier ~4.7e-4). Those IM/CRS results rest on asymptotic Gaussianity or symmetry of group-level statistics with large within-group samples, not on few draws per group from finite populations. Abstract/secondary-source reading only for IM and CRS.
verdict_C: NOT FOUND for the finite-sample-guarantee comparison; PARTLY for the design-comparison theme. Broska & Howes arXiv:2610.09601 (full text grepped) compare labelling designs (many labels in few clusters vs few labels in many clusters, fully vs partially labelled clusters) only through asymptotic variance as G->inf and explicitly defer small-sample/few-labelled-cluster corrections; Kluger et al. 2025 (described there) handle whole-cluster labelling by bootstrap; StratPPI (arXiv:2406.04291, full text grepped) states its guarantees are asymptotic; Mozer arXiv:2603.19160 (full text grepped) has no cluster/finite-sample content; Rosenblum & van der Laan 2009 give bounded-support tail-bound CIs for few-cluster survey sampling (not scale-equivariant, no stratified comparison). No source found comparing one-stage cluster labelling against within-cluster stratified labelling in terms of which designs can carry finite-sample guarantees (the ACS example: 5 persons/state vs >=11 of 51 states). Provisional: Kluger et al. was not located directly.
